newsitem.title: USA: Kemper Re to take EMLICO appeal to Privy Council.
newsitem.headline: Kemper Re to take EMLICO appeal to Privy Council.

text.p: Kemper Reinsurance Co. said Thursday it will appeal a Bermuda court's refusal to grant a judicial review of EMLICO's relocation to the highest court of appeal for British dependent territories.
Long Grove, Illinois-based Kemper Re, a unit of Kemper Insurance Co., said it will apply to the Bermuda Court of Appeal for permission to appeal to the Privy Council in London.
If permission is denied, Kemper Re said it will apply directly to the Privy Council for the right to appeal.
At issue is whether EMLICO, or Electric Mutual Liability Insurance Co. Ltd, acted fraudulently in 1995 when it moved to Bermuda from Massachusetts.
EMLICO, whose sole policyholder was Connecticut-based General Electric Co, filed a petition for voluntary winding up shortly after moving to Bermuda from Massachusetts.
Kemper Re said it was "optimistic that it will eventually overcome the procedural hurdles which have thus far prevented it from having a trial on the merits of the allegations of fraud."
Kemper Re feels the Bermuda courts have rejected its arguments because of legal technicalities, rather than on the merits of the case.

"EMLICO has done all it can in the Bermuda and Massachusetts courts to avoid any evidentiary hearing of the fraud allegations," said Richard Marcus, chief underwriting and claims counsel for Kemper Re. "No ruling by any court has cast any doubt on the strength of Kemper Re's case that EMLICO's redomestication to Bermuda was procured by fraud."
Kemper is among the reinsurers embroiled in litigation over EMLICO's liquidation, which may affect how soon the claims of EMLICO's 400 reinsurers might be resolved.

The case -- which pits General Electric, EMLICO, regulators and liquidators against some of the world's biggest reinsurers -- is significant because it might affect the degree to which insurers may restructure themselves in the face of massive environmental claims.
A Massachusetts Supreme Court justice is expected to rule soon on whether the state's insurance commissioner will be appointed U.S. receiver of EMLICO.
